correctness.rationale: The conditional-Poisson PGF is exact, with the first generation included and index case excluded. For 0<a<b a strictly decreasing positive exponential difference proves the strict generating-function order. For any c,d>0 an explicit large-z Chernoff bound yields log tail at most -n log log n+n log d+o(n); the event K=floor(n/log n), Y=n-K with independent conditional Poisson probabilities and Stirling estimates yields the matching lower bound. Subtraction proves the tail-ratio root limit b/a>1 and the eventual reverse ordering for every sufficiently high threshold. Normalization, parameter positivity, and branching reservoir scope were checked; 646 finite numerical checks corroborate coefficients but are not used for infinite assertions.

originality.rationale: This is a novel combination at the examined-source level, rather than a claim to invent PGFs, compound Poisson distributions or intervention metric disagreements. The available motivating primary manuscript and relevant statistical papers were compared by mathematical implications, not titles. No inspected result was found that subsumes the two-parameter, two-generation swap theorem including the sharp asymptotic upper-tail ratio. A potentially relevant older Neyman type-A paper is incompletely accessible, creating a disclosed priority risk.
residual_risks: Complete text of Zheng (1995), a potentially relevant Neyman type-A asymptotic paper, was not accessible; priority over more general light-tail compound-Poisson asymptotics is not established.
Generality of the theorem is limited to two generations and Poisson branching, and does not by itself give a finite-population epidemic claim.
Failure to identify a directly covering theorem in accessible searches is not a mathematical proof of first publication or uniqueness.

value.rationale: Generation-sensitive epidemic interventions pose a natural decision conflict between expected outbreak burden and low-probability extreme outcomes. Under exactly the same two reproduction intensities in opposite epochs, the sharp root tail ratio b/a and opposite strict generating-function ranking quantify a precise structural risk inversion across ALL ordered positive parameter pairs. This is substantially more informative than a numerical crossing, trivial expectation comparison, or an arbitrary finite-tail value. It provides a testable analytical benchmark, while explicitly not asserting finite-network risk or real-world policy optimality.
